originality.rationale: Primary full text of arXiv:1406.3958 and a full related uniform-composition RESULT.md were compared statement by statement. They own the run encoding and uniform-cut/maximum-part coupling, which are not claimed as novel. The contribution isolates an all-strictly-convex degree-index order and an exact first-Zagreb/diameter regression, covariance, variance and persistent bivariate Gaussian correlation not stated in those sources. Novelty is best-knowledge and qualified by complete-model encoding and historical-priority risks.
residual_risks: Acan--Hitczenko's full run encoding logically permits these deductions. Conditional majorization uses an already known uniform-cut coupling, so its independent conceptual novelty is limited to a strict whole-degree-vector lift.
An earlier weighted-composition CLT or degree-index analysis might encode identical covariance or the constant -sqrt(2/3) under another name; historical priority cannot be exhaustively certified.
General composition-CLT results were inspected only in opening material, not every technical appendix; no complete NOT_COVERING claim is made for that source.

value.rationale: This is a nontrivial all-n dependence analysis of two intrinsic but different random-tree invariants: diameter is global geometry, squared degree is local heterogeneity. It gives a full degree-vector convex-order coupling and exact finite regression rather than isolated small-number computations. The covariance scales linearly and the correlation tends to -sqrt(2/3), unlike many decorrelating random-tree statistic pairs. The exact variance and renewal-reward CLT are relevant for assessing joint asymptotic fluctuation and cannot be read from a fixed-m degree-frequency CLT without tail control.
